// https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-AXIOS-7361793

// https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/6463

  

import axios from '../../../index.js';

import http from 'http';

import assert from 'assert';

  

const GOOD\_PORT \= 4666;

const BAD\_PORT \= 4667;

  

describe('Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)', () \=> {

let goodServer, badServer;

  

beforeEach(() \=> {

goodServer \= http.createServer(function (req, res) {

res.write('good');

res.end();

}).listen(GOOD\_PORT);

badServer \= http.createServer(function (req, res) {

res.write('bad');

res.end();

}).listen(BAD\_PORT);

})

  

afterEach(() \=> {

goodServer.close();

badServer.close();

});

  

it('should not fetch bad server', async () \=> {

const ssrfAxios \= axios.create({

baseURL: 'http://localhost:' + String(GOOD\_PORT),

});

  

// Good payload would be \`userId = '12345'\`

// Malicious payload is as below.

const userId \= '/localhost:' + String(BAD\_PORT);

  

const response \= await ssrfAxios.get(\`/${userId}\`);

assert.strictEqual(response.data, 'good');

assert.strictEqual(response.config.baseURL, 'http://localhost:' + String(GOOD\_PORT));

assert.strictEqual(response.config.url, '//localhost:' + String(BAD\_PORT));

assert.strictEqual(response.request.res.responseUrl, 'http://localhost:' + String(GOOD\_PORT) + '/localhost:' + String(BAD\_PORT));

});

});

part.text:
Fix complete. Summary:

- **Change**: `lib/helpers/isAbsoluteURL.js` no longer treats protocol-relative URLs (starting with `//`) as absolute. Previously it returned `true` for them, which made `buildFullPath` bypass `baseURL` and pass `//host` straight to `new URL(fullPath, 'http://localhost')` in the http adapter (`lib/adapters/http.js:232`), letting an attacker redirect server-side requests to arbitrary hosts (CVE-2024-39338). Now `//...` URLs are combined with the configured `baseURL`.

- **Validation** (in the container):
  - SSRF regression test `test/unit/regression/SNYK-JS-AXIOS-7361793.js` passes (it was failing before the fix).
  - Full unit suite: 188 passing; the only failure is "should support HTTPS protocol", a pre-existing environmental timeout (it requests `https://www.google.com` and the container has no external network — confirmed failing on the unmodified baseline too).
  - `eslint lib/helpers/isAbsoluteURL.js` clean.
